terra.problem: The Lord orders the pillars to be toppled; the verse does not say that they then come down.
The verse says the thresholds shake, not that the whole place shakes. It also gives an order to strike the pillars rather than reporting that they are struck.
The passage does not say the Lord is at the bottom of the sea or that a serpent is already waiting there.
The joke compares Papa's difficulty touching a hot sheet directly with the Lord touching the earth. Comparisons must stay on the human side of the moment.
The timer joke compares Papa's difficulty getting something to listen with the Lord summoning the sea. Comparisons must stay on the human side of the moment.
The verse says no pebble will reach the ground. It does not say that nothing slips through the sieve.
The explanation says all the pebbles falling is the opposite of what one would expect, then says the verse flips that expectation too. The comparison contradicts itself.
